text.p: Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Production and Distribution Hartarto said on Wednesday the government supported a restructuring plan proposed by PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa.
"The government as one of the shareholders will enjoy the benefits of this restructuring," Hartarto told reporters after a meeting with President Suharto.

"The restructuring of PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa and the sale of the shares of PT Indofood Sukses Makmur to QAF Ltd, a publicly-listed company in Singapore, is part of a strategy to seize global marketing opportunities," Hartarto said.
He said the final result of the restructuring would be a net capital inflow of 1.7 trillion rupiah in foriegn exchange.

He said although the effect of the restructuring will be to give control of Indofood to QAF, the ultimate control of QAF is in the hands of Indonesians through majority ownership positions held by PT Mekar Perkasa, PT Citrabuana Dirgapuri and PT Kaolin Indah Utama, all units of the Salim Group.
"The final decision to carry out the restructuring is in the hands of the owners of Indocement," Hartarto added.
"The directors of the Salim Group have given assurances that the net capital receipts of the sale of Indofood will be invested domestically," he said.

He said the government has noted the commitment of the Salim Group to the developing the Indonesian economy in the form of various projects including palm oil plantations, sugar factories and development of new rice paddy fields in Kalimantan province.
Indocement said on July 15 its proposal to sell its 50.1 percent stake in Indofood, mostly to QAF, was aimed at focusing on its core cement business.
Indocement, Indofood and QAF are controlled by the Salim Group, Indonesia's largest conglomerate.
The restructuring plan had triggered loud criticism by local businessmen and economists who had said it would lead to an outflow of capital from Indonesia.
